BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary points

- **The Seller's "FINAL" label and "settled at principal level" language don't bind us.** Under playbook 0.4 and 6.3, a position is agreed only through our own authority process. Nothing in the file shows Amelia Frost approved any of these terms. The "market standard" preamble is the Seller's assertion, not verified evidence, so we should not rely on it.
- **The 20% / AUD 4.8M cap matches our conditional fallback, but that is not clearance.** The fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given. The Seller pairs the number with 18 months, AUD 25k/250k thresholds and excess-only recovery, all outside our fallbacks.
- **The disclosure facts are dated 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago.** Bluefen consent status, the Riverlark payout figure, the bonus position, and the DD-006 investigation should all be refreshed before we respond.

## Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8M | 25% / AUD 6M (20% fallback only with written authority) | Departure; not authorised |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Significant departure |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded (tipping) | Major departure |
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with written approval) | Departure; not authorised |
| Fundamental/Title | Same cap and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Core departure |
| Fraud carve-out | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable | Critical omission |
| Disclosure | Whole data room, public registers, Accounts, statutory registers | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject |
| Buyer knowledge | Bars claims for any matter known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion; named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject |
| Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; consent satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject |
| Riverlark | Release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject |
| Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | AUD 420k plus on-costs as specific line item or seller-funded | Reject |
| Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 AUD 180k; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure | Reject |
| DD-006 | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach either way | Reframe |
| Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Assess |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Open; no unlimited liability, no resolution assumed; separate categories | Reject |
| Title | DD-012 share register | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence | Reject as sole source |

## Material issues and reasoning

**1. Fraud carve-out is missing (critical).** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 would stop a buyer from recovering for fraud or deliberate concealment, even against non-reliance and exclusive-remedy language. Our playbook says no one may waive this. This is a non-negotiable deletion or carve-out, and the Seller's market-standard argument does not change it.

**2. Thresholds and caps stack against us.** Take a AUD 300,000 aggregate loss. Under the Seller's excess-only AUD 250,000 basket, the Seller pays AUD 50,000. Under our AUD 50,000 first-dollar tipping basket, the Seller pays the full AUD 300,000 (subject to the cap). The AUD 25,000 de minimis would also exclude many individually small but collectively material claims. Combined with the 18-month period, the Seller's package would substantially reduce recoverable exposure across the general warranties.

**3. Collapsing title and capacity into the general regime.** Title and capacity are the fundamental protections for what we are buying. Subjecting them to a 20% cap and 18-month period means a title defect could be time-barred or capped well below price. Our playbook keeps Fundamental/Title separate, at 100% and at least six years. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify this.

**4. Disclosure and buyer knowledge are linked and dangerous together.** Clause 1.1 discloses everything in the data room, and clause 8.3 bars claims for anything "discoverable". Together they let the Seller argue that anything in a 1,000-document room was disclosed against us. Specific fair disclosure is the standard. Blanket disclosure of data room, public registers and the Accounts should be rejected, and clause 8.3 should be deleted or limited as the playbook requires.

**5. Bluefen consent is a completion risk.** Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6M of FY26 revenue (about 30%). The disclosure states that no final written consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions has been provided. Treating consent as "satisfied on delivery" and offering only reasonable endeavours would let us complete without the consent and without knowing whether its conditions are met. We should require effective written consent and evidence of satisfied conditions as a Completion deliverable, or a price/indemnity mechanism if it cannot be obtained.

**6. Riverlark debt must be repaid at Completion.** About AUD 3.2M is outstanding and not repaid. A post-Completion release leaves the security over the business in place after we pay for it. The debt should be treated as Debt, paid directly from Completion funds, with releases delivered at Completion. If a post-Completion release is unavoidable, it needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**7. Bonuses are missing from the funds flow.** The AUD 420,000 bonuses are conditional, tied to Completion and continued employment, and are not in the funds flow. The disclosure also does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. Excluding them silently would leave us funding them. They should be a specific line item or seller-funded, with an on-cost estimate. The Seller's statement that this is "a matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism.

**8. Ironquay indemnity is too narrow.** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 fee. The DD-010 AUD 180,000 is unverified: the disclosure confirms it is not bank verification of non-payment, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. Our playbook says not to treat the figure as established either way. We should broaden the indemnity to cover third-party claims over the Project Materials and cure costs, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism. Independent verification of payment status should be obtained.

**9. DD-006 export incident.** The Seller calls this "not expected to be material", which goes beyond what the disclosure supports. The facts are that about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) may have been sent to an unintended external address, and whether anyone accessed them is unknown. We should not assume a breach, harm, or a notification duty, and should not accept a numeric loss figure either way. We should require log preservation, an investigation timetable, and regular updates. Privacy counsel should assess whether notification obligations could apply under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and whether a specific indemnity is needed. Including a specific indemnity goes beyond the playbook and should be discussed internally.

**10. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Seller describes these as ordinary course. The disclosure says it is not stated whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Per the playbook, we should assess them and not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct from price.

**11. Lease, Mossvale and other consents.** The lease notification (DD-007) and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) do not say whether landlord or counterparty consent is required for a share sale. We should ask for a legal confirmation from the Seller and obtain our own reading of each provision before Completion.

**12. Title is not independently proven.** The DD-012 register is an internal Seller-supplied source, so it is not independent evidence. The playbook requires independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. Practical steps include searches of the Personal Property Securities Register for encumbrances, verification of the share transfer chain and any stamp duty, board and shareholder authorisations, and a Seller warranty backed by a Fundamental/Title indemnity.

**13. Tax and IP remain open.** The Seller treats these as settled under the general regime. Our playbook keeps them open and separate. We should not accept any cap, time limit or disclosure regime that carries over from the general warranties, and should assume no unlimited liability and no resolution until we have agreed terms through the authority process.

## Recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL" and "not to be re-opened" framing.** Respond that the terms are under negotiation and that the Seller's market-standard and principal-level assertions are not accepted.
2. **Restore the fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
3. **Reset the general terms:** 25% / AUD 6M cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24-month claims period. Do not offer the 20%/18-month fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
4. **Separate Fundamental/Title** at 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Replace whole-data-room and public-register disclosure** with specific fair disclosure. Delete or narrow clause 8.3 so that named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry apply, and never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
6. **Bluefen:** require effective written consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion, or an agreed remedy.
7. **Riverlark:** require a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
8. **Bonuses:** add AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or make them seller-funded. Get an on-cost estimate.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and obtain independent verification of the AUD 180,000 status.
10. **DD-006:** require log preservation, an investigation plan and timetable, and regular updates. Obtain privacy advice. Make no assumption of breach or loss.
11. **Sandbar, lease and Mossvale:** request assessment and legal confirmation. No automatic debt classification or price deduction for Sandbar.
12. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. Treat DD-012 as supporting material only.
13. **Tax and IP:** keep open, separate from the general regime, with no unlimited liability or resolution assumed.
14. **Refresh all disclosed facts** as at the current date and confirm with Amelia Frost which items need her written approval before we send the mark-up.
